item.title: Xabi Alonso rules out January exit for Chelsea prodigy amid Barcelona links
item.description: Xabi Alonso rules out January exit for Chelsea prodigy amid Barcelona links Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has moved to close the doors on the possibility of a January exit for Brazilian wonderkid Estevao, amid links to Barcelona. The 19-year-old attacking prodigy has struggled for minutes in the early parts of the season, leading to speculations about a possible January exit. Barcelona keeping tabs on Estevao And Barça, who have monitored him since his days at Palmeiras, were said to keeping an eye on the situation . The Blaugrana looked into the possibility of signing Estevao seriously before he eventually joined Chelsea last year. One of the primary reasons behind the Catalans’ decision to not pursue the Brazilian gem was that he occupies the same position as Lamine Yamal. Back on Barcelona’s radar. (Photo by Andrew Redington/Getty Images) “There are several reasons. First, in the construction phase we are in, we have a player for the same position with similar characteristics named Lamine Yamal. It’s obvious,” Deco explained in an interview earlier this year. The 19-year-old enjoyed a productive debut season at Chelsea, but has found minutes hard to come by under Alonso this season. Up until today’s game against Manchester United, he had played less than 50 minutes of football in the Premier League this term. He was completely overlooked in the Blues’ Carabao Cup loss to Liverpool earlier in the week, sparking fresh questions over his future. Barcelona, as such, are understood to have taken note of the situation and are said to be closely monitoring any developments. Alonso shuts the door However, Alonso has moved to close the doors on any potential January departure for Estevao, stating that the youngster remains a part of his plans. Estevao not leaving in January, insists Alonso. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) “Yes, of course he’ll play. It’s a long season and there’ll be opportunities for everyone,” the Chelsea manager said, as quoted by SPORT . “It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch; they want to play. And when one of them hasn’t had enough playing time because of a decision I’ve made, I have to take responsibility for the fact that he isn’t as happy as he could be,” he further explained. Firmly ruling out a January exit, he clarified: “No, there are no discussions about that.” Alonso’s comments suggest that Chelsea are committed to giving Estevao time to establish himself. Whether that translates into a more substantial role on the pitch remains to be seen, particularly with Barcelona continuing to monitor his development.

item.description: The Green Bay Packers had the worst rushing offense in the NFL before Josh Jacobs returned to the field. Since he has come back from his stay on the commissioner’s exempt list, nothing has improved. Even after their win on Thursday Night Football, Green Bay is still averaging just 60.6 rushing yards a game, and Jacobs is averaging a woeful 2.3 yards per carry. Jacobs’ stay on the aforementioned exempt list was due to his arrest and eventual plea of no contest on charges of domestic violence. His continued presence on the Packers roster is a source of controversy surrounding the team, as many fans want Green Bay to part ways with him. item.description: City make 10 changes - Haaland, Bouaddi and Nunes all start Enzo Maresca has made 10 changes from our midweek win over Brighton. Ayyoub Bouaddi is the only player to retain his place from our Carabao Cup win over the Seagulls as the boss starts with a largely fresh XI. Matheus Nunes makes a welcome return after missing several games with injury. Tactics Though the personnel is much-changed, the style of play is likely to be the same as Wednesday’s Carabao Cup clash between the two teams. Brighton were a constant threat down the flanks in that game, and their fast-paced passing and movement off the ball will once again be a threat in this game. Gianluigi Donnarumma returns in goal in what will be a 4-3-3 formation. Nunes resumes at right-back, with Abdukodir Khusanov and Ruben Dias in central defence and Josko Gvardiol at left-back. In midfield, Bouaddi and Elliot Anderson are likely to protect the back four with Enzo Fernandez playing in a more advanced No.10 role. Our front three will be Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku on either flank and Erling Haaland through the middle. City looking to bounce back Though our penalty shoot-out win over Brighton was enjoyable and most welcome in midweek, the Premier League will always take precedence for the Blues. The 2-1 loss away to Aston Villa was disappointing given the opportunities we created, so getting back to winning ways this afternoon and consolidating top spot in the table. Today we face a Brighton side who have started the season in superb fashion, scoring goals and conceding few. Just as Wednesday’s game was, this will be a tough 90 minutes against a very good side who will be a threat from start to finish. Almost to a man, their players were snapping at our heels each and every time we were in possession, perhaps being more than a little fortunate not to have been penalised more than they were for some of the challenges. Maresca will want his players to match that aggression, move the ball quickly and try not to invite too much pressure when playing from the back. The Blues will have a largely rested starting XI given the wholesale changes in midweek, but the Seagulls will also have several players returning with fresh legs. It will be lively, open and you’d imagine there will be goals in what is likely to be rollercoaster-paced game. item.description: Kagiso Rabada took three wickets in the first half an hour to put South Africa on their way to victory [Getty Images] Third Test, Cape Town (day five of five) South Africa 329 & 387: Mulder 115, Rickelton 101 Australia 429 & 111: Lyon 33*; Rabada 3-39; Harmer 6-16 South Africa won by 176 runs; won series 2-1 Scorecard David Warner labelled Australia "terrible", "utterly disgraceful" and "un-Australian" as his former side crumbled under the pressure of a final-day chase and allowed South Africa to charge to a famous Test and series victory in Cape Town. Chasing 288 to win an enthralling contest themselves, Australia lost two wickets in the first over bowled by Kagiso Rabada and never recovered. Rabada was irresistible, also adding the key wicket of Travis Head caught at slip in a superb first spell to become the fastest bowler to 350 Test wickets. But Australia played a part in their own downfall, with Josh Inglis run out for four after inexplicably being called through by Cameron Green. That opened the door to spinner Simon Harmer, who had Alex Carey caught reverse sweeping with just two to his name and Cooper Connolly caught behind for a two-ball duck. At 60-7 at lunch, former opener Warner, who retired from Test cricket in January 2024, tore into his former team-mates. "It is terrible," he said on Fox Sports. "It is un-Australian. There is no fight whatsoever. It is disgraceful. "The batters have let the bowlers down all series. [Matt] Renshaw showed fight in that first Test but I think the batters have been utterly disgraceful." Australia then dropped anchor in a bizarre period - one scoring shot came in 50 minutes - but Harmer was not to be denied, taking the final wicket for career-best figures of 6-16 as Australia were dismissed for 111. Defeat comes at the start of an intense run of Test cricket for Pat Cummins' side, with attention now turning to four Tests at home against New Zealand starting in December before a five-Test tour of India, the 150th anniversary Test against England in March and next summer's Ashes. The consequences could be significant. South Africa's fine victory, earned across three fascinatingly fluctuating Tests, means the Proteas regain their position at the top of the world rankings and reaffirms their status as one of the world's very best sides. item.title: Colts willing to trade RB Jonathan Taylor, per report
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are now willing to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor , per a report from Adam Schefter of ESPN . Schefter adds in his report that the New York Giants are among the teams thought to have at least “some level of interest” in trading for Taylor. Schefter also lists the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers as teams believed to be interested in trading for Taylor. It’s no secret that while new Giants head coach John Harbaugh likes the trio of Cam Skattebo , Tyrone Tracy , and Devin Singletary , he has coveted a “bellcow” running back. The Giants reportedly pursued Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III in free agency and it was likewise reported that star Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love was tied with Arvell Reese at the top of their board. It was widely believed that the Giants would have drafted Love at fifth overall if he was still available. One of the issues with the Giants’ backfield is that while they lack an explosive option out of the backfield, and Taylor has been one of the NFL’s most explosive runners. Last year he was tied for sixth in the NFL with 16 designed runs of 15+ yards, and was third in “breakaway” runs. He also led the NFL with 18 rushing touchdowns to just two (2) fumbles last year. Our own Ed Valentine wrote earlier this week that the Giants should capitalize on their opportunit y to win the NFC East this year and go all-in on the 27-year old Taylor. After a report that head coach John Harbaugh personally called Tennessee Titans ownership in an effort to get defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons , who landed with the Chicago Bears, you can expect the Giants to be aggressive in pursuit of Taylor. The move would likely cost significant draft capital, possibly a first round pick to replace the one the Colts traded to the New York Jets. That’s real consideration oncern in a 2027 draft class that’s shaping up to be very talented and deep at a number of positions of need for the Giants. Acquiring Taylor would also require significant cap space and financial maneuvering. However, the argument is that Taylor is among the very best runners in the NFL and could complete a true “three headed monster” with wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely. And frankly, if Taylor becomes the apple of Harbaugh’s eye, it becomes Joe Schoen’s job to do everything in his power to acquire the running back. So what do you think Giants’ fans? Do you think the Giants are serious contenders for Taylor? And should they be?

item.title: Arsenal u18s win 10-goal thriller
item.description: Arsenal u18s win 10-goal thriller Arsenal Under-18s made it seven wins in a row with a wild 6-4 victory over Brentford. Photo via Arsenal.com Arsenal Under-18s made it seven wins in a row in all competitions after beating Brentford 6-4 in a remarkable 10-goal game. Vincent Joseph scored a first-half hat-trick, Maalik Hashi struck twice and Patrick Stachow added the other as Arsenal held off a Brentford side inspired by their own hattrick grabber, Jai Nwosu . The win moved Arsenal up to third in the table and continued an excellent run of form, although they were made to work for it. Arsenal started brightly, with Elyon Mbala winning the ball high up the pitch before getting to the byline and setting up Joseph for a simple finish with just three minutes on the clock. Brentford responded quickly. Teshaun Murisa brought down Andrew Noni inside the area and Nwosu converted the resulting penalty just six minutes later. After 10 minutes without a goal, the visitors then went ahead after a defensive mistake allowed Nwosu to round Charlie Phillips and score his second. Arsenal did not stay behind for long. Almost immediately, Joseph was brought down by Josh Oladapo-Gamu , with Hashi stepping up to put the penalty into the top corner just two minutes after they’d fallen behind. Five minutes later, Joseph restored Arsenal’s lead after Hashi’s free-kick came back off the post, reacting quickest to score his second of the game. His hat-trick arrived as they headed into added time. Murisa found Joseph inside the area, with the forward finishing to send Arsenal into the break 4-2 ahead. If anyone expected that to calm things down, it did not. Nwosu completed his own hat-trick just eight minutes after the restart, collecting a loose ball before finishing across goal. Again, Arsenal restored their two-goal advantage quickly, although they did take four minutes this time. Luis Munoz delivered a corner, Murisa headed it down and Stachow flicked the ball towards goal to make it 5-3. Still Brentford would not stop, but the goals did at least slow down. Nwosu (or Jovan Kasujja *) scored Brentford’s fourth despite pressure from Dan McCarron , cutting Arsenal’s lead back to a single goal with 25 minutes remaining. With 15 minutes remaining, Hashi finally gave Arsenal some breathing room after combining with substitute Emerson Nwaneri . Nwaneri broke down the left and pulled the ball back for Hashi, who finished for Arsenal’s sixth. Even then, Brentford thought they had found another way back into it when Nwosu put the ball in the net again, but the goal was ruled out for offside, denying the Bees a fifth. *Arsenal’s match report says Nwosu scored Brentford’s fourth but their tweets during the game, and the Opta stats , say Kasujja . item.description: Real Madrid forward keeps transfer options open despite improved role under Mourinho After a somewhat shaky start to the 2026-27 season, Real Madrid have clearly turned their form around in the last few weeks. The comeback win against AS Roma has turned out to be quite a turning point for the Merengues, and a clear sign of this was their victory against a FC Barcelona side in their last week’s El Clasico that had almost a perfect start to the season. One of the players who proved decisive in the important game against AS Roma was the Brazilian forward Endrick. He had played only four minutes prior to that game, against Elche, but was still at his best level as he helped his team turn the score around and get a win in Rome . That performance significantly improved Endrick’s prospects in Mourinho’s plans. After playing only four minutes in the first eight games of the season, he has played 102 minutes in the last five games. Still, he is not a regular starter for the Portuguese coach and is not expected to become one, especially because of all the attacking talent present in the Real Madrid squad. Meanwhile, the Brazilian remains a highly sought player in the market. Several clubs are keeping a close eye on his situation as they want to sign him in January. For his part, Diario AS reports that Endrick is keeping his options open, and has not yet made a final decision. Before making a decision about a move in January, the forward wants to exhaust all his options with Mourinho. Going forward, there are around ten games, seven in La Liga and three in the Champions League, left before the start of the transfer window, and these games will significantly impact the decision the Brazilian makes about a winter transfer. In recent days, Jose Mourinho has assured that he is not considering a departure for Endrick, but the player wants to play regularly to continue his growth and development, and it remains to be seen whether he will remain at Real Madrid for the second half of this season.

item.title: Detroit Lions Have One Major Advantage Against Vikings’ Terrifying Defense
item.description: The Detroit Lions are about to face the most aggressive defense in the NFL, but there’s one major reason to believe Jared Goff and company could have an advantage in Sunday’s showdown against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Goff has been one of the NFL’s most effective quarterbacks against the blitz this season. That’s particularly important considering Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores is blitzing at a rate the league has rarely seen. And if the Vikings continue sending extra rushers at the same staggering pace, Detroit’s offense could have opportunities to make them pay. Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) talks to center Graham Glasgow (60) before a play against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, November 2, 2025. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jared Goff Has Been Outstanding Against the Blitz Minnesota enters Sunday’s matchup at 6-0, largely because of a defense that has been overwhelming opposing quarterbacks. The Vikings have blitzed on approximately 70% of defensive dropbacks this season , easily the highest rate in the NFL. Washington ranks second at approximately 43%. Minnesota also leads the league in scoring defense, allowing just 12.3 points per game. But here’s where things get interesting for Detroit. Goff has completed 70% of his passes against the blitz for 605 yards, six touchdowns, and zero interceptions , producing a 123.3 passer rating in those situations. Those numbers are remarkable considering how difficult the Vikings have made life for opposing quarterbacks. Detroit’s quarterback also enters the matchup with 14 touchdown passes and zero interceptions through six games, demonstrating the kind of decision-making that will be essential against Flores’ unpredictable defense. The matchup has become especially intriguing because Goff has already demonstrated an ability to punish aggressive defenses throughout the season. Minnesota may be the most difficult test yet, but Goff has the experience and production to give Detroit a legitimate chance. Why Vikings’ Aggressive Defense Could Backfire Against Detroit The Vikings aren’t simply blitzing more often than everyone else. They’re disguising pressure, changing coverage responsibilities, and forcing quarterbacks to identify where defenders will be coming from before the snap. Minnesota blitzed Indianapolis on more than 85% of its dropbacks last Sunday , the highest single-game rate recorded during the NFL’s Next Gen Stats era. That approach helped limit the Colts to just 108 passing yards. But Detroit has something Indianapolis struggled to provide. An explosive passing attack capable of punishing defenses when they leave receivers in favorable matchups. Jameson Williams has been particularly dangerous lately, recording seven receptions for 138 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games. His speed creates an obvious challenge when defensive backs are asked to defend without consistent help

item.title: ‘I truly do regret it’ – Stephen A. Smith issues public apology to former NBA No. 1 pick
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Stephen A. Smith rarely walks back a take, but nearly two decades later, one infamous on-air evisceration still haunts him. Kwame Brown was thrust into an unforgiving spotlight in 2001 when Michael Jordan drafted him straight out of high school as Washington’s number-one overall pick. Carrying the franchise’s future proved overwhelming, and after turbulent stints with the Wizards and Lakers, Brown became the poster child for modern NBA draft busts. And the defining moment of his public ridicule came in 2008 when Los Angeles shipped him to Memphis for Pau Gasol. On live television, Stephen A. Smith unleashed a merciless on-air takedown, famously branding Brown a “bonafide scrub” who couldn’t play a lick of basketball. Stephen A. Smith apologises to Kwame Brown Stephen A. Smith almost never backs down, but after years of watching Kwame Brown get dragged across the internet, he’s finally owning his part in it. He admitted his brutal takedown went too far, conceding that turning a struggling young player into a permanent punchline still sits uncomfortably with him. He said on his YouTube channel : “I will always regret the impact that I had on Kwame Brown. I never meant for that to happen; I was just covering the sport. I said what I said at the time when he was playing and much younger, and I never thought it would materialize into becoming a meme 16 or 18 years later. I never anticipated that, so I truly do regret it. “That’s number one. That is why, no matter what he says, I really don’t say anything back. I don’t bother him because people have bothered him enough. I can understand his frustration—I really, really do. I respect the brother as a man, and I never wished any of that on him.” Despite the unrelenting “bust” label, Brown persevered, carving out a 12-season NBA career across seven different franchises. And he eventually snapped in 2021, launching viral YouTube videos targeting Smith directly, calling him a media bully who profited off tearing down a young teenager for decades. item.title: Juventus vs Napoli: Classic match - Tactical thunder and the dawn of a dynasty in Turin
item.description: FC Juventus v SSC Napoli - Serie A - Getty Images Sport Relive the explosive 2012 encounter where Juventus broke a tactical deadlock with two goals in two minutes. Martin Caceres and a teenage Paul Pogba secured a vital 2-0 victory that defined the Scudetto race. On 20 October 2012, the Juventus Stadium was not merely a football ground; it was a pressure cooker. Matchday 8 of the Serie A season brought together two sides locked at the summit, both boasting identical records of six wins and a draw. Antonio Conte’s Juventus were the undefeated champions seeking validation, while Walter Mazzarri’s Napoli arrived as the ferocious challengers, desperate to shift the balance of power from North to South. The air in Turin was thick with the scent of a title decider played in the autumn chill. A tactical chess match on a razor edge The opening eighty minutes were a masterclass in defensive rigidity and tactical stifling. Bianconeri deployed their iconic BBC triumvirate - Andrea Barzagli, Leonardo Bonucci, and Giorgio Chiellini - to nullify the threat of Edinson Cavani. Napoli nearly shattered the script in the 26th minute when Cavani’s vicious free kick beat Marco Storari, only to rattle the woodwork. It was a game of suffocating spaces, where every pass from Andrea Pirlo was met by a wall of blue, and every surge from Marek Hamsik was tracked with industrial diligence. Ten minutes of fury break the deadlock As the match drifted toward what many expected to be a pragmatic stalemate, Conte looked to his bench for inspiration. The deadlock finally fractured in the 80th minute. Pirlo, the game’s ultimate architect, swung a trademark corner into the corridor of uncertainty. Caceres, who had only recently entered the fray, rose with predatory timing to thump a header past Morgan De Sanctis. The stadium erupted, a cacophony of relief and triumph that signaled the shifting tectonic plates of the season. The arrival of a teenage phenomenon Before the visitors could reorganise their shattered lines, Juve struck again just two minutes later. A clearance fell to a 19-year-old Pogba at the edge of the area. In a moment of pure, unadulterated technique, the young Frenchman met the dropping ball with a high volley. The strike was true, arrowing into the bottom corner and leaving De Sanctis helpless. It was more than just a goal; it was the arrival of a global superstar and the definitive knockout blow for the Neapolitan challenge. Securing the throne in Turin The 2-0 scoreline was a testament to the clinical nature of Conte’s machine. While Napoli had competed man-for-man for the vast majority of the contest, Bianconeri proved they possessed the depth and the mental fortitude to seize the marginal gains. The victory moved the Bianconeri three points clear at the top of the table, establishing a lead they would never relinquish. It was the afternoon the tactical deadlock was broken by raw, individual brilliance, leaving the visitors to contemplate what might have been.

item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - FEBRUARY 2: DeForest Buckner #99 of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the sideline before the game against the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIV at Hard Rock Stadium on February 2, 2020 in Miami, Florida. The San Francisco 49ers now have four players who left, either in free agency or via trade, and eventually made their way back to Santa Clara. You might see one or two players return to their original team, but not at the rate the 49ers have. There are two ways to look at this. The first is that the 49ers are a first-class organization. While wide receiver Mike Evans wanted to play with Brock Purdy , George Kittle sold him on it with all the things the 49ers do differently . It was either more modern technology, personalized nutritionists instead of a team nutritionist, or other small things that cost a lot of money and don’t show up on a salary cap sheet. The second: the grass isn’t always greener elsewhere. That’s not to say there aren’t grievances from the 49ers’ returning players. Dre Greenlaw had some choice words for Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton, but it’s not so much an indictment that other teams are worse, just that the 49ers do something right. Greenlaw left for a three-year, $35 million deal in Denver. This resulted in eight games and a release after one season. A r elease he felt was handled poorly . Then there’s Samuel. He was traded to the Washington Commanders and got a crowd-pleasing 17 carries. This is after he averaged around 45 a season over his previous four years with the 49ers. Same player, different usage. The time away was so short that Samuel said he felt like he never left . And finally, Buckner. The latest addition of returning players . The Chicago Bears were reportedly interested in the defensive tackle in this week’s NFC arms race. Buckner himself wanted San Francisco . Long-time bullpen coach Ben Fritz has agreed to become the pitching coach for the Arizona Diamondbacks, which no doubt hurts San Diego and will likely help Arizona. Fritz had been a mainstay in the Padres’ organization despite numerous managers taking the head position in the locker room. item.description: The Mbappe-Vinicius paradox: 13 assists, but Real Madrid’s big dilemma remains One of the most debated topics at Real Madrid since 2024 has been the attacking partnership between Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr. Both extraordinary players in their own right, the duo have given Los Blancos ‘ managers a nightmare when it comes to fitting them into the same XI while maintaining the right balance. Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa all tried in vain, and the latest to be tasked with the unenviable responsibility is Portuguese manager Jose Mourinho. Despite obvious concerns on the pitch, there is one statistic that might come as a surprise regarding the attacking duo. Vinicius has provided 13 assists for Mbappe’s first 100 Real Madrid goals . That is more than any other teammate, with Arda Guler following with 12. Vinicius remains Mbappe’s leading provider Mbappe reached 100 goals for Real Madrid with his brace against Barcelona last weekend. The Frenchman reached the milestone in just 116 appearances. Of those goals, the Brazilian has directly created 13%. Guler’s numbers don’t come as a surprise considering his excellent relationship with the Frenchman. However, the relationship between Vinicius and Mbappe is worth examining more closely. Mbappe has provided four assists for the Brazilian over the same period. On the surface, these numbers challenge the argument that the pair don’t have an understanding on the pitch. In theory, you can see why the partnership should work. Vinicius can attract defenders before releasing Mbappe into space. Similarly, the Frenchman can also lay off chances for his teammate. The individual connection seems to exist. The bigger question is why those moments have not consistently translated into better collective performances for the team. Why their partnership remains a tactical problem The difficulty becomes apparent when taking a closer look at Real Madrid’s performances against stronger opponents. Both players naturally prefer to attack from the left, with Mbappe drifting away from his central position rather frequently. This takes him into the same areas Vinicius naturally likes to occupy, resulting in an imbalance in the attacking structure. This problem was evident during Real Madrid’s 2-1 loss to Atletico Madrid in September . The average position map from the game showed Vinicius invisible in Mbappe’s shadow. That picture, in a nutshell, encapsulates the Brazilian’s Real Madrid career ever since Mbappe came to Spain. Instead of two attacking superstars stretching opposition defences, Los Blancos become too predictable, and opponents know exactly how to stop them.
